text:
### Observed differences

- The three alternatives A14, A16 and A19 — exactly one of which runs in each case in both windows — changed their common successor: before, all of their outgoing transitions led to A20; in the later window, all of them lead to A25. [DIR010, DIR012, DIR015, REL002, REL005, REL018]
- The cluster A15/A17/A18, whose members occur together in every case in both windows, switched in the opposite direction: before, about 30–38% of each member's outgoing transitions went to A25 and none to A20; in the later window, none go to A25 and about 28–36% go to A20. [DIR011, DIR013, DIR014, REL011]
- The two feeding activities swapped which group they supply: A24 sent about 37%/33%/30% of its transitions to A15/A18/A17 before, but about 39%/33%/29% to A19/A14/A16 in the later window; A35 sent about 35%/30%/36% to A16/A14/A19 before and about 36%/33%/31% to A17/A15/A18 in the later window. [DIR017, DIR026]
- The two groups exchanged their typical place in the case: A14, A16 and A19 moved from a median position of about one-third (0.33–0.35) to about two-thirds (0.68–0.69) of the trace, while A15, A17 and A18 moved from about 0.64 to about 0.38; A20 (0.37 → 0.44) and A24 (0.57 → 0.64) shifted slightly later, while A25 (about 0.70) and A35 (about 0.31) stayed where they were. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008, POS009, POS010]
- Cross-group ordering reversed completely: before, A14/A16/A19 preceded A15/A17/A18, A20 and A24 in every joint appearance (e.g., A14 before A15 in 30% of cases, never the reverse); in the later window the cluster precedes the alternatives, and the cluster precedes A20 and A24, which had preceded it in 100% of joint appearances before. Within the cluster, A15/A17/A18 keep an unfixed, mixed order in both windows (A15 before A17 in 55% before, 46% after). [REL001, REL003, REL004, REL006, REL007, REL010, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL019, REL020, REL024, REL025, REL026, REL027, REL028, REL029, REL030, REL031, REL011, REL012, REL023]
- Step distances flipped accordingly: A24 reached A25 four steps later in every case before and two steps in the later window; A35 reached A20 two steps before and four steps in the later window. [LAG007, LAG008]
- Participation of all involved activities stayed essentially stable (A15/A17/A18 in all 200 traces in both windows; A14 about 30 → 33, A16 about 35 → 29, A19 about 36 → 39 per 100 cases), so the rewiring is not accompanied by activities appearing, disappearing or repeating differently. [OCC013, OCC014, OCC015, POS002, POS004, POS005]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that two groups of activities exchanged their places in the case: the mutually exclusive alternatives A14/A16/A19 and the always-together cluster A15/A17/A18 swapped slots. Before, the alternatives ran in the earlier part of the case — fed by A35 and followed by A20 — while the cluster ran later, fed by A24 and followed by A25; in the later window the cluster runs between A35 and A20 and the alternatives between A24 and A25. The change is shown directly and consistently: successor relations flipped categorically, median positions moved by about a third of the trace, every cross-group order relation reversed with the old order dropping to zero, and the A24→A25 and A35→A20 step distances flipped between 4 and 2 — differences larger than in about 199 of 200 random re-splits. Stable participation of every involved activity argues against activities being added, removed, made optional or repeated differently; note that the many agreeing items largely re-describe one underlying rewiring rather than independent confirmations. A competing reading the evidence cannot exclude is that the two groups are parallel segments that merely exchanged the order in which they execute rather than being relocated; also, positions are event positions, so nothing can be said about clock time. [DIR010, DIR011, DIR012, DIR013, DIR014, DIR015, DIR017, DIR026, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008, REL001, REL014, REL015, REL025, REL028, LAG007, LAG008, OCC013, OCC014, OCC015]

Other differences:
- A34 occurs more often (participation about 48.5 → 56.5 per 100 cases; mean occurrences 0.78 → 0.89), and A11 directs a larger share of its transitions to A34 (about 30% → 37%). [OCC021, DIR009]
- Around A36–A39: A36's exits shifted from A38 (about 52% → 46%) toward A37 (about 48% → 54%); A37 participation rose (about 61.5 → 66.5 per 100 cases) while A38 and A39 fell (about 62 → 59.5) with fewer repeats. [OCC023, OCC024, OCC025, DIR027]
- A29's exits shifted from A26 (about 54% → 43%) toward A30 (about 46% → 57%). [DIR021, DIR022]
- Several early activities show small participation shifts of about 5 per 100 cases in both directions (A01, A03, A04, A05 up; A02, A06, A07, A08, A12 down). [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC011]
